alignments.note: Waw of the pair And now takes And (rule 14).
The discourse adverb takes the word writing its own lexeme, now (rule 14).
The single fronted copula of this verbless question is both the construction's copula and the question auxiliary, and belongs to the interrogative particle (rule 20).
Proper name; the copula is the particle's.
Noun rendered kinsman; its possessive is the suffix's.
Relative plus the resumptive suffix on maidens, which points at the antecedent Boaz, are rendered by one whose and share a unit headed on the relative (rule 22).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun, headed on wast.
The preposition H854 with, not the object marker.
Participial predicate rendered by the finite winnoweth.

The ASV demotes the marked object to a locative phrase and writes in before it; the marker takes that word, since the marked noun keeps its own English and nothing else answers for the preposition (rule 16). Marking the marker unrepresented and the in added was the competing reading.
Construct noun threshing floor; head on floor as the noun of the compound, with threshing the competing head.
The article stands on the rectum, which the ASV renders anarthrously, so it takes the phrase's fronted the (rule 29).
Rectum rendered barley, promoted to the English object.

Article and night jointly render to night, the fixed expression naming the current definite night under rule 30. Excluding the article and assigning the whole phrase to an adverbial accusative was considered, but leaves that expressed determination unaccounted for.

review_notes: The whose of with whose maidens fuses the relative with the resumptive 3ms suffix, which agrees with and denotes Boaz (rule 22).
The supplied in before the threshing floor is given to the object marker standing on that noun rather than left added; the alternative is noted on the unit.
